hints.title: Separate slope from bending
hints.body: A trapezium uses the chord joining two sampled points. Whether it overestimates depends on that chord being above the curve, not on whether the curve rises or falls.
hints.pitfall: A decreasing curve can give either kind of estimate.
hints.pause: Sketch one upward-bending and one downward-bending arc with a chord.

recall.reminder: Determine over- or underestimation from chord position relative to the curve.

hints.title: Interpret the signs and directions
hints.body: Relate the sign of the second derivative to the two chord sketches. Translate if and only if into their separate implication directions.
hints.recap: A geometric estimate and a logical direction both have to match.
hints.pitfall: A sufficient condition does not automatically become a necessary condition.
hints.pause: Determine which derivative assumptions guarantee the stated error.

recall.reminder: A geometric estimate and a logical direction both have to match.
New learning: the second derivative measures the change of gradient; connect that change to the chord sketch.

hints.title: Test a claimed necessity
hints.body: Try <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>. Compare its trapezium chords with the graph and examine the derivative sign across the interval.
hints.recap: To test necessity, seek the target behaviour without the alleged requirement.
hints.pitfall: Check the full interval instead of just one derivative value.
hints.pause: Use this example and your chord sketches to evaluate every offered implication.

recall.reminder: To test necessity, seek the target behaviour without the alleged requirement.

solution:
If f″(x)>0 throughout the interval, the graph bends upward and every trapezium chord lies above the curve between its endpoints. Adding the strip areas gives an overestimate. Therefore the condition f′(x)<0 and f″(x)>0 is sufficient, as D asserts; the negative-slope part is more than is needed.

A is false: f(x)=1−x2 on [−1,0] is positive in the interior, has f′>0 and f″<0, yet its chords lie below the graph, producing an underestimate.

B, C, E and F each claim that a particular strict slope sign is necessary. The function f(x)=x2+1 on [−1,1] gives an overestimate but its derivative 2x changes sign, so none of those necessity claims can hold.

Answer D.
knowledgePattern: Separate sufficient convexity from unnecessary gradient sign
